items.question: How early does my Arc thermostat start heating before a scheduled temperature change?
items.answer: If Lead Time is turned on, Arc starts heating or cooling up to 45 minutes before a scheduled temperature change.

sources.title: Away mode and arrival detection
sources.text:
Away mode saves energy while nobody is home by holding your Arc thermostat at its Away temperatures instead of following your schedule. You can set Away temperatures under Settings > Comfort > Away temperatures; the defaults are 16 degrees C for heating and 28 degrees C for cooling.

Arc can switch to Away mode on its own using arrival detection. Arrival detection uses the location of phones that have the Tessaline Home app installed and location access set to Always. When every phone in your home has been outside the home zone for at least 20 minutes, Arc switches to Away. When the first phone comes back inside the home zone, Arc leaves Away mode and returns to your schedule.

You can set the size of the home zone anywhere from 150 metres to 2 kilometres. A larger zone gives your system more time to reach a comfortable temperature before you walk in, but Arc may also leave Away mode when someone is only passing nearby.

To switch Away mode on or off yourself, tap the house icon on the app's home screen. A manual change overrides arrival detection until the next time everyone leaves or someone arrives.

sources.title: Lead Time on Arc thermostats
sources.text:
Lead Time helps your home reach a scheduled temperature at the time you scheduled it, rather than starting to heat or cool only when the schedule changes over. You can turn it on or off at any time: open the Tessaline Home app, tap your thermostat, and go to Settings > Comfort > Lead Time.

If Lead Time is turned on, Arc starts heating or cooling up to 45 minutes before a scheduled temperature change. During its first seven days, Arc measures how quickly your home warms up and cools down, so early starts may be short at first and become more accurate over time. The exact start time also varies from day to day with the outdoor temperature.

Lead Time only applies to changes that come from your schedule. Temperatures you set by hand on the dial or in the app take effect straight away and are never started early. Lead Time is not available while Arc is in Emergency Heat, and it pauses automatically whenever Away mode is active.

If your system seems to start far too early, check that the postcode under Settings > Location is correct, because Arc uses it to look up the outdoor temperature.

sources.title: Filter change reminders
sources.text:
Arc can remind you when it is time to change the air filter in your heating and cooling system. Reminders are based on how many hours your system has actually run, not on calendar days, so a mild season stretches the time between reminders.

By default, Arc reminds you after 500 hours of fan run time. If your filter's packaging recommends a different interval, change it under Settings > Equipment > Filter reminder. You can choose any value from 100 to 1,500 hours in steps of 50.

When a reminder is due, a banner appears in the Tessaline Home app and a small filter icon appears on the thermostat's display. After you replace the filter, tap Reset on the banner, or press and hold the filter icon on Arc for three seconds, to start counting again.

If you have more than one Arc in your home, each thermostat keeps its own count. Turning filter reminders off does not change your schedule or any other setting.

items.question: Do I have to turn on two-step verification for my Corvane account?
items.answer: Starting 2 March 2026, the Corvane app requires two-step verification for account owners who have invited shared users.

sources.title: Adding and removing shared users
sources.text:
You can share your Vista Doorbell with the people you live with so they can see who is at the door. Go to Account > Household, tap Invite, and enter the person's email address. They receive an invitation that stays valid for 7 days; if it expires, send a new one from the same screen.

Each account can have up to 8 shared users. Shared users can watch live video, view recorded clips, talk through the doorbell, and receive motion and ring alerts. They cannot change device settings, delete clips, manage your subscription, or invite other people.

To remove someone, open Account > Household, tap their name, and choose Remove. They lose access straight away. Any clips they downloaded to their own phone before you removed them stay on their phone.

If a shared user says they cannot see your doorbell, ask them to check that they accepted the invitation using the same email address you entered. Invitations cannot be moved from one email address to another.

sources.title: Resetting your Corvane password
sources.text:
If you have forgotten your password, tap Forgot password on the sign-in screen of the Corvane app and enter the email address on your account. We send you a reset link that works once and expires after 60 minutes.

Your new password must be at least 10 characters long and cannot match any of your last five passwords. After you change it, every phone and browser signed in to your account is signed out, including the Corvane app on your own phone, so you will need to sign in again.

Changing your password does not affect your shared users. They keep their access and continue to sign in with their own details.

If the reset email does not arrive within a few minutes, check your spam or junk folder, and make sure you entered the address you used when you created the account. For security reasons, Corvane support cannot set a password for you or tell you your password over the phone.

sources.title: Two-step verification for your Corvane account
sources.text:
Two-step verification adds a second check when someone signs in to your Corvane account. After entering your password, you confirm the sign-in with a six-digit code, either sent to you by text message or generated in an authenticator app.

Starting 2 March 2026, the Corvane app requires two-step verification for account owners who have invited shared users. Shared users are people you have added under Account > Household so that they can watch live video from your Vista Doorbell and receive its alerts. If this applies to you and you have not set up two-step verification by that date, the app asks you to set it up the next time you sign in, and live video stays locked until you finish.

To set it up at any time, go to Account > Security > Two-step verification and follow the prompts.

When you finish setup, the app shows ten single-use backup codes. Keep them somewhere safe and away from your phone: if you lose access to your phone, a backup code lets you sign in once. You can generate a new set at any time from the same screen, and doing so cancels any codes you have not used.

Shared users sign in with their own Corvane accounts. Their security settings are separate from yours, and turning on two-step verification for your account does not change how they sign in.

items.question: Can I get a free battery pack because firmware 3.8 drained my Keyway battery?
items.answer: Between 1 September and 30 November 2026, owners of the Keyway Pro can request one free rechargeable battery pack per lock.

sources.title: Faster battery drain after firmware 3.8
sources.text:
Some Keyway locks that installed firmware 3.8 in July 2026 used up their batteries much faster than usual, because the lock was checking for nearby phones far more often than it needed to. Firmware 3.9 fixes the battery drain for both the Keyway Pro and the Keyway Classic. It installs automatically overnight; to check your version, open the Pellora app and go to Lock > Settings > About.

To make up for the extra battery use, we are offering affected owners a replacement.

Between 1 September and 30 November 2026, owners of the Keyway Pro can request one free rechargeable battery pack per lock. The Keyway Classic runs on four AA batteries instead of a battery pack, so during the same period Classic owners can claim a refund of up to 12 euros per lock for replacement batteries, with proof of purchase.

To make a request, open the Pellora app, choose the lock, and tap Help > Battery offer. You need to be the lock's owner; people with guest or family access cannot make a request. Each lock can receive the offer only once, even if it changes owner.

sources.title: Charging the Keyway Pro battery pack
sources.text:
The Keyway Pro is powered by a rechargeable battery pack that slides out of the inside part of the lock. A full charge usually lasts between four and six months, depending on how often the door is locked and unlocked and how many people in your home use Auto-Unlock.

When the pack drops to 15 percent, the Pellora app sends a low-battery alert and the keypad light flashes amber after each use. At 5 percent, the lock stops using Auto-Unlock to save power, but you can still lock and unlock it with the app, the keypad or the key.

To charge it, press the release tab, slide the pack out, and connect it to a USB-C charger. Charging from empty takes about three hours, and the light on the pack turns solid green when it is full. While the pack is out, the lock cannot be operated electronically, so keep your physical key handy or charge the pack while you are at home.

A spare pack lets you swap without waiting. Spare packs are sold separately in the Pellora app under Shop.

sources.title: Replacing the batteries in a Keyway Classic
sources.text:
The Keyway Classic uses four AA alkaline or lithium batteries. Do not use rechargeable AA batteries, because their lower voltage can make the low-battery warning appear too late.

The Pellora app shows the remaining battery level on the lock's main screen. When it falls to 20 percent you get a low-battery alert, and the lock beeps three times after each use. At that point you will usually still have a few weeks of normal use.

To replace the batteries, slide the inside cover upwards to remove it, take out the old batteries, and insert the new ones so that they match the plus and minus symbols in the holder. Your settings, access codes and schedules are kept while the batteries are out.

If the batteries run completely flat, you can still open the door with the physical key, or hold a 9-volt battery against the two contacts under the outside keypad to power the lock for long enough to enter your code.

The Keyway Pro is powered by a rechargeable battery pack that slides out of the inside part of the lock. A full charge usually lasts between four and six months, depending on how often the door is locked and unlocked and how many people in your home use Auto-Unlock.

When the pack drops to 15 percent, the Pellora app sends a low-battery alert and the keypad light flashes amber after each use. At 5 percent, the lock stops using Auto-Unlock to save power, but you can still lock and unlock it with the app, the keypad or the key.

To charge it, press the release tab, slide the pack out, and connect it to a USB-C charger. Charging from empty takes about three hours, and the light on the pack turns solid green when it is full. While the pack is out, the lock cannot be operated electronically, so keep your physical key handy or charge the pack while you are at home.

A spare pack lets you swap without waiting. Spare packs are sold separately in the Pellora app under Shop.

sources.title: Replacing the batteries in a Keyway Classic
sources.text:
The Keyway Classic uses four AA alkaline or lithium batteries. Do not use rechargeable AA batteries, because their lower voltage can make the low-battery warning appear too late.

The Pellora app shows the remaining battery level on the lock's main screen. When it falls to 20 percent you get a low-battery alert, and the lock beeps three times after each use. At that point you will usually still have a few weeks of normal use.

To replace the batteries, slide the inside cover upwards to remove it, take out the old batteries, and insert the new ones so that they match the plus and minus symbols in the holder. Your settings, access codes and schedules are kept while the batteries are out.

If the batteries run completely flat, you can still open the door with the physical key, or hold a 9-volt battery against the two contacts under the outside keypad to power the lock for long enough to enter your code.

construction.note: Plausible offer-page claim; S1 explains how to request the pack but not delivery, S2 only says spare packs are sold in the Shop, and S3 covers AA replacement. No passage gives shipping times.

sources.title: Faster battery drain after firmware 3.8
sources.text:
Some Keyway locks that installed firmware 3.8 in July 2026 used up their batteries much faster than usual, because the lock was checking for nearby phones far more often than it needed to. Firmware 3.9 fixes the battery drain for both the Keyway Pro and the Keyway Classic. It installs automatically overnight; to check your version, open the Pellora app and go to Lock > Settings > About.

To make up for the extra battery use, we are offering affected owners a replacement.

Between 1 September and 30 November 2026, owners of the Keyway Pro can request one free rechargeable battery pack per lock. The Keyway Classic runs on four AA batteries instead of a battery pack, so during the same period Classic owners can claim a refund of up to 12 euros per lock for replacement batteries, with proof of purchase.

To make a request, open the Pellora app, choose the lock, and tap Help > Battery offer. You need to be the lock's owner; people with guest or family access cannot make a request. Each lock can receive the offer only once, even if it changes owner.

items.question: Will my Myrtlewick automations keep working if my internet goes down?
items.answer: With Local Mode switched on, automations between devices connected to the hub keep running when your internet connection is down.

sources.title: What the light on your Myrtlewick Hub means
sources.text:
The ring of light on the front of the Myrtlewick Hub shows what the hub is doing.

Solid white: the hub is connected to your network and to the Myrtlewick cloud.
Slow blue pulse: the hub is ready to be set up, or is waiting for you to finish adding a device.
Solid yellow: the hub is connected to your network but cannot reach the internet. Check your router; if other devices in your home are online, restart the hub by unplugging it for ten seconds.
Flashing yellow: the hub cannot connect to your Wi-Fi network. This often happens after a router is replaced or its password is changed. Use Hub > Network > Change Wi-Fi in the app to reconnect.
Solid purple: a firmware update is installing. Do not unplug the hub until the light turns white again, which usually takes less than ten minutes.
Red: the hub has a hardware fault. Contact Myrtlewick support and have the serial number from the base of the hub ready.

You can dim the light, or turn it off overnight, under Hub > Settings > Light.

sources.title: Connecting the hub with an Ethernet cable
sources.text:
The Myrtlewick Hub can connect to your router over Wi-Fi or with an Ethernet cable. A wired connection is usually more stable, especially if the hub sits far from your router or in a room with thick walls.

To switch to Ethernet, plug a network cable into the port on the back of the hub and the other end into a free port on your router. The hub detects the cable within about 30 seconds and switches over automatically; you do not need to change anything in the app. If you unplug the cable later, the hub goes back to the last Wi-Fi network it used.

The Ethernet port supports speeds of up to 100 Mbps, which is far more than the hub needs. Power over Ethernet is not supported, so the hub always needs its own power adapter.

If the light stays solid yellow after you connect the cable, try a different port on your router or a different cable.

sources.title: Using the Myrtlewick Hub without an internet connection
sources.text:
Most Myrtlewick Hub features run through our cloud service, but some can keep working entirely inside your home. Local Mode is an optional setting: to turn it on, open the Myrtlewick app and go to Hub > Advanced > Local Mode. The hub restarts once when you change this setting, which takes about two minutes.

With Local Mode switched on, automations between devices connected to the hub keep running when your internet connection is down. This includes schedules, scenes triggered by sensors, and presses of Myrtlewick wall buttons. Automations that rely on an outside service, such as sunrise times, weather conditions or a voice assistant, need the internet in every case and pause until your connection is back.

While the internet is down, you can still control devices from the app if your phone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the hub. Remote access from outside your home is not available, and notifications that would have been sent during the outage are not stored or delivered later.

When the connection returns, the hub uploads the events it recorded during the outage to your activity log within 15 minutes.

construction.note: Base claim: the Local Mode sentence of S3 copied verbatim, keeping the 'With Local Mode switched on' condition.

items.question: Is Ondrel deleting my old alarm history?
items.answer: All alarm events recorded between 1 January 2023 and 31 May 2024 will be permanently deleted on 1 December 2026.

sources.title: How long camera clips are kept
sources.text:
Clips from Wardline cameras are saved to the cloud when motion is detected or an alarm goes off. How long they are kept depends on your plan.

Wardline Essentials keeps clips for 7 days. Wardline Plus keeps clips for 30 days, and Wardline Pro Monitoring keeps them for 60 days. Clips recorded during an alarm are kept for 90 days on every plan, so that you have time to share them with your insurer or the police.

When you change plan, the new retention period applies to clips recorded after the change. Clips you already have keep the retention period they were saved with.

To keep a clip for longer, open it in the History tab and tap Download. Downloaded clips are saved to your phone and are not deleted when the cloud copy expires. Deleting a clip in the app removes the cloud copy only; anything you have downloaded stays on your device.

sources.title: Changes to alarm history in the Ondrel app
sources.text:
We are moving alarm history to a new storage system so that the History tab loads faster and can be searched.

All alarm events recorded between 1 January 2023 and 31 May 2024 will be permanently deleted on 1 December 2026. Once they are deleted, Ondrel support cannot recover them.

If you want to keep a copy of these events, download them before the deletion date. In the app, go to Settings > Account > Download my data and choose Alarm history. The file arrives by email as a CSV within 24 hours. Each download covers up to 12 months of events, so you may need to request more than one.

This change affects alarm events only: arming and disarming, sensor triggers, panic button presses and siren activations. Camera clips are stored separately and follow the retention period of your plan.

Only the account owner can request a download. Shared users can still view alarm history in the app but cannot export it.

sources.title: Arming your system on a schedule
sources.text:
An arming schedule sets your Wardline system to Home or Away automatically at the times you choose, so you do not have to remember to arm it every night.

To create one, go to Settings > Security > Arming schedule and tap Add. Choose the mode, the time and the days of the week. You can add up to 6 schedules per system. Schedules follow the time zone set for your home, not the time zone of your phone.

Five minutes before a scheduled arming, everyone on the account who has notifications turned on receives a reminder. If a door or window is open at that time, the system arms anyway and leaves that sensor out until it is closed, and the app tells you which sensor was skipped.

Schedules can only arm the system. Disarming always needs a code, the app or a key fob, so a schedule will never disarm Wardline for you.

standalone.question: Can I check on my Myrtlewick Hub remotely while my internet is down? Please cite your sources.
standalone.answer: While your internet connection is down, remote access to the hub from outside your home is not available [S1].

sources.title: What the light on your Myrtlewick Hub means
sources.text:
The ring of light on the front of the Myrtlewick Hub shows what the hub is doing.

Solid white: the hub is connected to your network and to the Myrtlewick cloud.
Slow blue pulse: the hub is ready to be set up, or is waiting for you to finish adding a device.
Solid yellow: the hub is connected to your network but cannot reach the internet. Check your router; if other devices in your home are online, restart the hub by unplugging it for ten seconds.
Flashing yellow: the hub cannot connect to your Wi-Fi network. This often happens after a router is replaced or its password is changed. Use Hub > Network > Change Wi-Fi in the app to reconnect.
Solid purple: a firmware update is installing. Do not unplug the hub until the light turns white again, which usually takes less than ten minutes.
Red: the hub has a hardware fault. Contact Myrtlewick support and have the serial number from the base of the hub ready.

You can dim the light, or turn it off overnight, under Hub > Settings > Light.

sources.title: Connecting the hub with an Ethernet cable
sources.text:
The Myrtlewick Hub can connect to your router over Wi-Fi or with an Ethernet cable. A wired connection is usually more stable, especially if the hub sits far from your router or in a room with thick walls.

To switch to Ethernet, plug a network cable into the port on the back of the hub and the other end into a free port on your router. The hub detects the cable within about 30 seconds and switches over automatically; you do not need to change anything in the app. If you unplug the cable later, the hub goes back to the last Wi-Fi network it used.

The Ethernet port supports speeds of up to 100 Mbps, which is far more than the hub needs. Power over Ethernet is not supported, so the hub always needs its own power adapter.

If the light stays solid yellow after you connect the cable, try a different port on your router or a different cable.

sources.title: Using the Myrtlewick Hub without an internet connection
sources.text:
Most Myrtlewick Hub features run through our cloud service, but some can keep working entirely inside your home. Local Mode is an optional setting: to turn it on, open the Myrtlewick app and go to Hub > Advanced > Local Mode. The hub restarts once when you change this setting, which takes about two minutes.

With Local Mode switched on, automations between devices connected to the hub keep running when your internet connection is down. This includes schedules, scenes triggered by sensors, and presses of Myrtlewick wall buttons. Automations that rely on an outside service, such as sunrise times, weather conditions or a voice assistant, need the internet in every case and pause until your connection is back.

While the internet is down, you can still control devices from the app if your phone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the hub. Remote access from outside your home is not available, and notifications that would have been sent during the outage are not stored or delivered later.

When the connection returns, the hub uploads the events it recorded during the outage to your activity log within 15 minutes.

You can share your Vista Doorbell with the people you live with so they can see who is at the door. Go to Account > Household, tap Invite, and enter the person's email address. They receive an invitation that stays valid for 7 days; if it expires, send a new one from the same screen.

To remove someone, open Account > Household, tap their name, and choose Remove. They lose access straight away. Any clips they downloaded to their own phone before you removed them stay on their phone.

Keep Multi costs 10 euros per month and covers every Corvane doorbell and camera at one address, with no limit on the number of devices. It saves 60 days of video history and includes everything in Keep Plus.

Prices include VAT, and both plans are billed monthly.

standalone.question: When did Lead Time start working with heat pumps?
standalone.answer: Lead Time gained support for heat pump systems in the Arc update released on 21 July 2026.

sources.title: Lead Time on Arc thermostats
sources.text:
Lead Time helps your home reach a scheduled temperature at the time you scheduled it, rather than starting to heat or cool only when the schedule changes over. You can turn it on or off at any time: open the Tessaline Home app, tap your thermostat, and go to Settings > Comfort > Lead Time.

If Lead Time is turned on, Arc starts heating or cooling up to 45 minutes before a scheduled temperature change. During its first seven days, Arc measures how quickly your home warms up and cools down, so early starts may be short at first and become more accurate over time. The exact start time also varies from day to day with the outdoor temperature.

Lead Time only applies to changes that come from your schedule. Temperatures you set by hand on the dial or in the app take effect straight away and are never started early. Lead Time is not available while Arc is in Emergency Heat, and it pauses automatically whenever Away mode is active.

If your system seems to start far too early, check that the postcode under Settings > Location is correct, because Arc uses it to look up the outdoor temperature.

sources.title: Arc thermostat software release notes
sources.text:

- Lead Time now supports heat pump systems, including those with auxiliary heat strips.
- Fixed an issue where the display could stay lit after a schedule change.

Version 5.3 - released 21 July 2026
- Added an indoor humidity reading to the home screen on models with a humidity sensor.
- Filter reminders can now be set in steps of 50 hours.

Version 5.2 - released 2 June 2026
- Away mode now waits 20 minutes after the last phone leaves before switching on, instead of 10 minutes.
- Improved Wi-Fi reconnection after a router restart.

Version 5.1 - released 14 April 2026
- Added Spanish and Portuguese as display languages.

standalone.question: I live in France. Can I get a free courier pickup to repair my Glide?
standalone.answer: Owners in France whose Glide is under warranty can request a free courier pickup for repairs.

sources.title: Getting your Glide vacuum repaired
sources.text:
If your Glide vacuum has a fault that the troubleshooting steps in the app do not fix, contact Brindlecove support from the app under Help > Contact us. Have the serial number ready; you can find it under the dustbin or in the app under Vacuum > Settings > About.

Glide vacuums come with a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. Owners in Germany and Austria whose Glide is under warranty can request a free courier pickup for repairs. The courier brings a box and packing materials, so you do not need to keep the original packaging.

Repairs usually take 7 to 10 working days from when we receive the vacuum. We return it with the same settings and maps, unless the main board had to be replaced, in which case you will need to map your home again.

Batteries, brushes and filters are wear parts and are covered by the warranty for the first six months only. You can buy replacements in the app under Shop.

sources.title: Obstacle photos on the Glide R6
sources.text:
The Glide R6 has a front camera that recognises obstacles such as cables, socks and pet waste, and steers around them. When it avoids something, it can take a photo so you can see what was in the way and tidy it up.

Obstacle photos stay off until you turn them on under Vacuum > Settings > Obstacle photos. Photos are stored on the vacuum itself and are deleted automatically after 7 days. They appear in the app only while your phone is on the same Wi-Fi network as the vacuum, and they are never uploaded to Brindlecove servers.

You can delete all photos at once from the same settings screen. Turning the feature off also deletes any photos that are still stored.

The camera keeps working to avoid obstacles whether or not photos are turned on. It does not record video and has no microphone. A small white light next to the camera comes on while a photo is being taken.

standalone.question: Will my Arc Plus warn me when the air in my home gets too dry?
standalone.answer: Arc Plus thermostats can send Dry Air alerts.

sources.title: Dry Air alerts
sources.text:
Dry Air alerts let you know when the air in your home is getting too dry, which often happens in winter when the heating runs for long periods. When indoor humidity stays below 30 percent for more than two hours, you get a notification in the Tessaline Home app with tips for raising it.

Dry Air alerts are available on Tessaline thermostats that have a built-in humidity sensor and are running software version 5.5 or later. To check your version, open the Tessaline Home app and go to Settings > About.

To turn the alerts on or off, go to Settings > Notifications > Dry Air. Only the person who set up the thermostat can change this setting, but once the alerts are on, everyone in the home receives them.

Dry Air alerts do not control humidifiers. If you have a whole-home humidifier, manage it with its own controls.

sources.title: Filter change reminders
sources.text:
Arc can remind you when it is time to change the air filter in your heating and cooling system. Reminders are based on how many hours your system has actually run, not on calendar days, so a mild season stretches the time between reminders.

By default, Arc reminds you after 500 hours of fan run time. If your filter's packaging recommends a different interval, change it under Settings > Equipment > Filter reminder. You can choose any value from 100 to 1,500 hours in steps of 50.

When a reminder is due, a banner appears in the Tessaline Home app and a small filter icon appears on the thermostat's display. After you replace the filter, tap Reset on the banner, or press and hold the filter icon on Arc for three seconds, to start counting again.

If you have more than one Arc in your home, each thermostat keeps its own count. Turning filter reminders off does not change your schedule or any other setting.

sources.title: Arc Plus at a glance
sources.text:
Arc Plus is the larger of our two thermostats. It has a 3.5-inch colour display, a built-in humidity sensor, and a presence sensor that wakes the display when you walk up to it. Like the standard Arc, it works with most gas, oil and electric heating systems, as well as central air conditioning and heat pumps.

Arc Plus comes with one Tessaline Room Sensor in the box. Place it in the room where you spend the most time, and Arc Plus can balance the temperature between that room and the hallway where the thermostat is mounted. You can add up to five more room sensors.

Arc Plus needs a common wire, often called a C-wire, for power. If your system does not have one, the Power Adapter Kit, sold separately in the Tessaline Home app, provides it.

Arc Plus comes in white, charcoal and brushed steel finishes.

gold.target_claim: Arc Plus thermostats can send Dry Air alerts.

gold_spans.quote: It has a 3.5-inch colour display, a built-in humidity sensor, and a presence sensor that wakes the display when you walk up to it.
Dry Air alerts are available on Tessaline thermostats that have a built-in humidity sensor and are running software version 5.5 or later.

construction.note: S3 gives Arc Plus a humidity sensor and S1 makes Dry Air alerts depend on that sensor plus software 5.5 or later; no passage says which software Arc Plus runs, so the claim needs the unstated bridge that it is on 5.5 or later.

standalone.question: How cold can it get before my Vista Doorbell stops working?
standalone.answer: The Vista Doorbell can operate in temperatures as low as -20 degrees C.

sources.title: Using your Vista Doorbell in cold weather
sources.text:
Cold weather affects every battery-powered device, and the Vista Doorbell is no exception. The Vista Doorbell is rated to operate in temperatures from -10 degrees C to 45 degrees C. During very cold spells you may notice the battery level dropping faster than usual, and the doorbell may take a second or two longer to start recording.

To get the most out of the battery in winter, lower the motion sensitivity so the doorbell wakes up less often, and turn off pre-roll recording under Device > Video settings.

The battery does not charge below 0 degrees C. If the app says the battery is too cold to charge, bring the doorbell indoors and let it warm up to room temperature before you plug it in.

If you live somewhere with long, hard winters, a wired installation avoids most battery problems. When the Vista Doorbell is wired to a doorbell transformer, it keeps its battery topped up and runs on mains power.

sources.title: Installing your Vista Doorbell
sources.text:
Before you start, charge the Vista Doorbell's battery fully using the USB-C cable in the box. A full charge takes about five hours, and the light ring turns solid green when it is done.

Choose a spot about 120 centimetres above the ground with a clear view of your path. The Vista Doorbell works in temperatures from -20 degrees C to 50 degrees C, so it can be fitted outdoors in most climates without a cover. Avoid places where it will be in direct sun for most of the day, because glare can make motion detection less reliable.

Use the mounting plate as a template to mark the screw holes. On brick or stone, drill with the 6 mm masonry bit included and use the wall plugs; on wood, screw straight in.

When the plate is fixed, clip the doorbell onto it and tighten the security screw at the bottom with the small screwdriver from the box. Then open the Corvane app and tap Add device to connect the doorbell to your Wi-Fi.

gold.target_claim: The Vista Doorbell can operate at temperatures as low as -20 degrees C.

gold_spans.quote: The Vista Doorbell works in temperatures from -20 degrees C to 50 degrees C
The Vista Doorbell is rated to operate in temperatures from -10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

construction.note: S2 gives an operating range down to -20 degrees C and S1 gives one down to -10 degrees C for the same doorbell; neither passage is dated or says it replaces the other, and the answer states the S2 value.

standalone.question: How many floor maps can my Glide R4 save?
standalone.answer: The Glide R4 can save up to 3 floor maps.

sources.title: Saving maps for more than one floor
sources.text:
Last updated: 4 November 2025

If your home has more than one floor, your Glide R4 can learn a separate map for each of them. Carry the vacuum to the new floor, place it on the floor away from the stairs, and start a mapping run from Map > New map in the Brindlecove app.

The Glide R4 can save up to 3 floor maps. When you start a clean, it compares what its sensors see with each saved map and picks the right one within the first minute, so you do not need to tell it which floor it is on.

Each saved map keeps its own rooms, no-go zones and cleaning schedule. Schedules only run on the floor where the dock is, because the vacuum cannot return to a dock on another floor.

To delete a map you no longer need, open it and choose Delete map from the menu.

sources.title: No-go zones and virtual walls
sources.text:
No-go zones keep your Glide vacuum out of areas you choose, such as a play mat or the space around a pet's water bowl. To add one, open the map in the Brindlecove app, tap Edit map, choose No-go zone, and drag the rectangle into place.

Each map can hold up to 10 no-go zones and 10 virtual walls. Virtual walls are straight lines the vacuum will not cross, which is useful for blocking a doorway without marking off a whole room.

Zones and walls are saved with the map. If the vacuum creates a new map, for example after a factory reset, you will need to draw them again.

If the vacuum keeps entering a no-go zone, check that its map is not out of date: moving large furniture can make it lose track of where it is. A quick mapping run from Map > Update map usually fixes this.

sources.title: Glide R4 firmware 2.8
sources.text:
Updated 12 May 2026

Firmware 2.8 is now available for every Glide R4. It installs automatically while the vacuum is docked and charging, and your saved maps, schedules and no-go zones are kept during the update.

What's new in 2.8:
- More saved maps. Firmware 2.8 raises the number of floor maps the Glide R4 can save from 3 to 5. This replaces the limit of 3 maps given in our earlier help articles.
- Quieter docking. The vacuum now slows down for the last 30 centimetres before it reaches the dock.
- Better edge cleaning. In Deep mode, the side brush spins faster along walls and skirting boards.

If your vacuum has not updated after a week, check that the dock is within range of your Wi-Fi and that the vacuum is switched on while it is docked.

gold.target_claim: The Glide R4 can save at most 3 floor maps.

gold_spans.quote: Firmware 2.8 raises the number of floor maps the Glide R4 can save from 3 to 5. This replaces the limit of 3 maps given in our earlier help articles.

construction.note: S1 (last updated 4 November 2025) gives a limit of 3 maps; S3 (updated 12 May 2026) raises it to 5 and explicitly replaces the earlier limit. The answer repeats the stale value.

standalone.question: How many people can I share my Corvane doorbell with? Please cite your sources.
standalone.answer: Each Corvane account can have up to 8 shared users [S3].

sources.title: Adding and removing shared users
sources.text:
You can share your Vista Doorbell with the people you live with so they can see who is at the door. Go to Account > Household, tap Invite, and enter the person's email address. They receive an invitation that stays valid for 7 days; if it expires, send a new one from the same screen.

Each account can have up to 8 shared users. Shared users can watch live video, view recorded clips, talk through the doorbell, and receive motion and ring alerts. They cannot change device settings, delete clips, manage your subscription, or invite other people.

To remove someone, open Account > Household, tap their name, and choose Remove. They lose access straight away. Any clips they downloaded to their own phone before you removed them stay on their phone.

If a shared user says they cannot see your doorbell, ask them to check that they accepted the invitation using the same email address you entered. Invitations cannot be moved from one email address to another.

sources.title: Resetting your Corvane password
sources.text:
If you have forgotten your password, tap Forgot password on the sign-in screen of the Corvane app and enter the email address on your account. We send you a reset link that works once and expires after 60 minutes.

Your new password must be at least 10 characters long and cannot match any of your last five passwords. After you change it, every phone and browser signed in to your account is signed out, including the Corvane app on your own phone, so you will need to sign in again.

Changing your password does not affect your shared users. They keep their access and continue to sign in with their own details.

If the reset email does not arrive within a few minutes, check your spam or junk folder, and make sure you entered the address you used when you created the account. For security reasons, Corvane support cannot set a password for you or tell you your password over the phone.

sources.title: Two-step verification for your Corvane account
sources.text:
Two-step verification adds a second check when someone signs in to your Corvane account. After entering your password, you confirm the sign-in with a six-digit code, either sent to you by text message or generated in an authenticator app.

Starting 2 March 2026, the Corvane app requires two-step verification for account owners who have invited shared users. Shared users are people you have added under Account > Household so that they can watch live video from your Vista Doorbell and receive its alerts. If this applies to you and you have not set up two-step verification by that date, the app asks you to set it up the next time you sign in, and live video stays locked until you finish.

To set it up at any time, go to Account > Security > Two-step verification and follow the prompts.

When you finish setup, the app shows ten single-use backup codes. Keep them somewhere safe and away from your phone: if you lose access to your phone, a backup code lets you sign in once. You can generate a new set at any time from the same screen, and doing so cancels any codes you have not used.

Shared users sign in with their own Corvane accounts. Their security settings are separate from yours, and turning on two-step verification for your account does not change how they sign in.

gold.target_claim: Each Corvane account can have up to 8 shared users.

gold_spans.quote: Each account can have up to 8 shared users.

construction.note: Claim is supported by S1 (shared users article) but cites S3, the two-step verification article, which discusses shared users without giving any limit on their number.

standalone.question: How much is the Wardline Pro Monitoring price going up?
standalone.answer: The new Wardline Pro Monitoring price is a 10 percent increase on the current monthly price.

sources.title: How long camera clips are kept
sources.text:
Clips from Wardline cameras are saved to the cloud when motion is detected or an alarm goes off. How long they are kept depends on your plan.

Wardline Essentials keeps clips for 7 days. Wardline Plus keeps clips for 30 days, and Wardline Pro Monitoring keeps them for 60 days. Clips recorded during an alarm are kept for 90 days on every plan, so that you have time to share them with your insurer or the police.

When you change plan, the new retention period applies to clips recorded after the change. Clips you already have keep the retention period they were saved with.

To keep a clip for longer, open it in the History tab and tap Download. Downloaded clips are saved to your phone and are not deleted when the cloud copy expires. Deleting a clip in the app removes the cloud copy only; anything you have downloaded stays on your device.

sources.title: Wardline plan prices from 1 January 2027

From 1 January 2027, prices for some Wardline plans are changing. We will write to every affected customer at least 30 days before their first bill at the new price.

New monthly prices:

You can see the price you pay today under Settings > Plan in the Ondrel app. If you would like to move to a different plan before the change, you can do so at any time from the same screen, with no fee.

standalone.question: If I create a guest code while I'm at work, will it work on my Keyway lock straight away?
standalone.answer: New guest codes work immediately on Keyway locks.

sources.title: Charging the Keyway Pro battery pack
sources.text:
The Keyway Pro is powered by a rechargeable battery pack that slides out of the inside part of the lock. A full charge usually lasts between four and six months, depending on how often the door is locked and unlocked and how many people in your home use Auto-Unlock.

When the pack drops to 15 percent, the Pellora app sends a low-battery alert and the keypad light flashes amber after each use. At 5 percent, the lock stops using Auto-Unlock to save power, but you can still lock and unlock it with the app, the keypad or the key.

To charge it, press the release tab, slide the pack out, and connect it to a USB-C charger. Charging from empty takes about three hours, and the light on the pack turns solid green when it is full. While the pack is out, the lock cannot be operated electronically, so keep your physical key handy or charge the pack while you are at home.

A spare pack lets you swap without waiting. Spare packs are sold separately in the Pellora app under Shop.

sources.title: Creating guest codes for your Keyway lock
sources.text:
Guest codes let visitors, cleaners or dog walkers open your door with the keypad, without needing the Pellora app. To create one, open the app, choose your lock, and tap Access > Guest codes > New code.

New guest codes work immediately, but only on locks that are within range of a Pellora Bridge. A lock without a bridge receives new codes the next time a phone with the Pellora app comes within Bluetooth range of it.

You can make a code permanent, limit it to certain days and times, or set it to expire after a single use. Each Keyway lock holds up to 30 guest codes at a time.

When someone uses a guest code, the lock's owner gets a notification showing the code's name, so give each code a name you will recognise. Deleting a code follows the same rule as creating one: it takes effect straight away on locks with a bridge, and otherwise the next time a phone with the app is nearby.

gold.target_claim: New guest codes work immediately on every Keyway lock.

gold_spans.quote: New guest codes work immediately, but only on locks that are within range of a Pellora Bridge.
